title: Staying in Chicago with his own combos and Paramount records
summary: After about eleven months the band returned to Louisville but Jones stayed, formed small combos, and played Kelly's Stable and the Sherman House. He describes the first and second groups (Turners, Elijah Cross, Heebie-Jeebies).

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: After they worked the Classic Cabaret for about eleven months, do you remember where you went then?
Oh, yeah. Were you, did you stay with the band?

No, the band left me here. Oh. The band left me, went on back to Louisville. I stayed here and made records with the Power Mount Company, and I had a band of my own, a little four piece and five piece, combo band. I played all around in the various night club, Kelly's Stable, Sherman House.

You played Sherman? Yeah, I played Sherman House. Yeah. All right. Then with that, with that group you made the Paramount record. Now that was your first group in about 1922, and Homer Brown Blues on Paramount and Tiger Rag on the reverse. This is the one with Ernest Tapley, Banjo, James Turner, guitar, Saul Turner. Was he a brother?
No, he was just a friend of ours.
Well, I mean the two Turners. I mean the two Turners.
Guitar and Harvey Jones. And then you had a second group. How much later was that?
That was about a year later.
You had a fellow named Heebie-Jeebies?
Elijah Cross. And you still had Sol Turner.
I suppose you did vocals too?
Oh, yeah. Actually, all four of us, three of us sang together. And what mostly I did was play this horn and my other horn, and sang and danced.
